title: SKU Sandbox & Rate Simulator for Token-Level Reconciliation
creator: Aisha Nambiar
description:
Problem: Customers need to reconcile runtime traces with line-item billing and to explore pricing policy effects on chargebacks. Existing console cost views show aggregates but don't let engineers or finance teams run hypotheses (e.g., quantization on a route, per-SKU amortization, or alternate rate bands) and then export invoice-ready rows.

Goal: Design an interactive "SKU Sandbox" that lets users: (1) map runtime traces and message slices to SKUs, (2) apply alternate rate bands or promos across a selectable time window, (3) preview how those policy changes would alter per-customer and per-route chargebacks, and (4) export either "invoice-ready" CSVs or developer-friendly raw trace bundles.

Scope: This ticket covers the console UX: Figma prototypes for the Sandbox panel, export schema options, compact SKU sparklines, a side-by-side simulator view for up to three rate scenarios, role-aware column selection for CSVs, and lightweight microcopy explaining assumptions (amortization method, attribution algorithm choice). Implementation tasks (ENG) and backend schema design are tracked as dependencies.

Design constraints & decisions: We avoid heavy sampling to preserve fidelity; the default view uses pre-aggregated 1-min buckets (backend provides). Attribution modes: session-level, message-level, and prefix-KV (fallthrough). The UI exposes an "explain" drawer that surfaces the attribution choices used in the current export. Exports contain two flavors: "Invoice-ready" (aggregated, customer-facing rows with SKUs, line-item rates, totals) and "Trace bundle" (raw records, token breakdowns, KV keys).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Prototype shows an interactive panel allowing selection of time window, up to 3 rate scenarios, and mapping rules for SKUs.
A2: Side-by-side preview updates within 750ms for typical time window (<= 7 days) using pre-aggregated buckets; visual diffs (delta column) appear clearly colored and sortable.
A3: Export options include two schemas (Invoice-ready, Trace bundle) and a role-aware column picker; sample CSV generated from prototype data must match backend schema provided by ENG-2109.
A4: Explain drawer displays chosen attribution algorithm and sample reconciled trace rows for auditability.
A5: Usability test (n=6: 3 engineers, 2 finance, 1 platform PM) median task time for "produce invoice CSV" <= 4 minutes with no critical errors.
A6: Design handoff assets (Figma frames, token specs, export schema) uploaded to Confluence and linked in this ticket.
